id: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)

facts.text: Serve the mains when Angel Eyes sits down to eat at the farmer's table.
facts.why: Wikipedia and Filmsite have Angel Eyes questioning the ex-Confederate Stevens and then shooting him and his son. Neither says he sits at the table and eats, so the meal cue could not be confirmed from the sources opened.
facts.fix: Serve the mains when Angel Eyes comes calling at the Stevens farm.

facts.text: Eat now, talk later. I don't trust a man who chats over his beans.
facts.why: Tuco never says this. It is invented. His real line about talking is the one to the one-armed man in the bathtub scene: 'When you have to shoot, shoot. Don't talk.'
facts.fix: When you have to shoot, shoot. Don't talk.

fix_note.text: When you have to shoot, shoot. Don't talk.

vibe.verdict: A proper dusty saloon bill with the Sad Hill name and Blondie's poncho, but the film's big set pieces are barely used.
missing: Tuco's hanging, with Blondie shooting the rope (the bounty scam)
The desert march after Blondie strands Tuco, and Tuco marching Blondie
Blowing up the bridge at Branston
The three-way standoff at Sad Hill (the poncho and the stone)
Tuco's bath scene (when you have to shoot, shoot)
The prison camp and Angel Eyes as a Union sergeant
ideas: Swap 'Desert crossing tortilla chips' for a name from Tuco marching Blondie across the desert, with a water jug garnish
Swap 'Gold coin potato rounds' for 'Arch Stanton's grave potatoes' (the name on the grave, the gold is in the one marked Unknown)
Swap the mousse cup name for 'Unknown Grave mousse' with the coin buried in it, which is where the gold really is
Add a bathtub drink or sweet with the real Tuco line 'When you have to shoot, shoot. Don't talk.'
